tasks.title: Building NTF_LED_TYPES
tasks.statement: You need the board LEDs (bit 0) and two more `AP_Notify` drivers: bits **{a}** and **{b}**. What value do you write to `NTF_LED_TYPES`?
tasks.solution: The value of a mask is the sum of 2^n over the bits that are set: 1 + 2^a + 2^b. Examples from the module: the board and NeoPixel (bit 8) give 1 + 256 = 257; the board, NeoPixel and ESC LEDs (bit 11) give 1 + 256 + 2048 = 2305. Bits 8 and 18 (NeoPixel and NeoPixelRGB) are not set together: it is one and the same output, and with both set bit 8 wins.

tasks.title: How many drivers in the mask
tasks.statement: `NTF_LED_TYPES = {v}`. How many LED drivers are enabled (how many of bits 0–19 are one)?
tasks.solution: Decompose the number into powers of two; each set bit is one driver. Examples from the module: 455 = 256 + 128 + 64 + 4 + 2 + 1 is six drivers (bits 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8); 123079 is nine (bits 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 15, 16); 647367 = 123079 + 524288 is ten.

tasks.title: Strip current in a status color
tasks.statement: A strip of **{n}** LEDs shows a color with this many channels lit: **{k}** (1 is red, green or blue; 2 is yellow; 3 is white). `NTF_LED_BRIGHT = {l}`. The course model: 20 mA per channel at brightness byte 255; the strip brightness bytes are 51, 127 and 255 for levels 1, 2 and 3. Find the strip current.
tasks.solution: I = N · k · 0.02 A · (brightness byte / 255). The module's example: 8 LEDs, yellow (2 channels), level 2 → 8 · 2 · 0.02 · 127 / 255 = 0.159 A. At full brightness in white this gives the course rule of 0.06 A per LED.

tasks.title: How many LEDs the BEC can carry
tasks.statement: A 5 V BEC is rated for **{b} A**, and the other loads of the branch draw **{i} A**. By the course rule (0.06 A per LED, BEC rating at least 1.5 × the sum of the branch currents) find the largest number of strip LEDs.
tasks.solution: The allowed sum for the branch is b / 1.5; that leaves b / 1.5 − i for the strip; divide by 0.06 A and drop the fraction. The module's example: a 2 A BEC, 0.9 A of other loads → 1.333 − 0.9 = 0.433 A → 7.2 → 7 LEDs; the eighth gives 1.5 · 1.38 = 2.07 A > 2 A. `NTF_LED_LEN` does not accept more than 32 on one output, so put a second strip on another output.
